label: Deaths (2026 Outbreak)
source: ECDC Ebola outbreak tracker (published 18 September) — data as of 16 September 2026
contestNote: Confirmed deaths: 3,605 DRC + 2 Uganda = 3,607 total as of 16 September (ECDC, published 18 September), a crude CFR of roughly 48.2%. label: Case Fatality Rate (2026 BDBV)
value: ~48.2% (DRC, crude, as of 16 Sept); ~61.3% in North Kivu province (as of 16 Sept)
source: ECDC Ebola outbreak tracker (published 18 September) — data as of 16 September 2026
contestNote: Crude national CFR calculated from reported confirmed cases/deaths; DRC's overall CFR has climbed from roughly 20% in early June to a peak near 48.6% in late August and stood at roughly 48.2% as of 16 September (7,475 cases / 3,605 deaths). Province-level variation remains stark: North Kivu (1,350 cases / 828 deaths as of 16 September) sits near 61.3%, well above the national average, which responders and outside experts attribute to weaker treatment access rather than a change in virus behavior. Africa CDC's Emergency Consultative Group noted 17 September that roughly 60% of reported deaths are still occurring in communities rather than health facilities, a proxy for gaps in case detection and treatment access. Africa CDC warned 22 August that if the official case count captures only 30-40% of true infections, the true CFR could be substantially lower than the crude reported figure. BDBV historically 25–47% CFR; this outbreak's crude national CFR now sits at or above the top of the historical range.

label: BDBV Vaccine Status — Over 3,000 Frontline Workers Vaccinated of 50,000 Target; Phase 3 Trial 'Within Weeks'
value: 3,000+ of 70,000 allocated Ervebo doses administered to frontline/health workers (target 50,000); 20,000 doses reserved for the Phase 3 trial, WHO says trial to begin 'within weeks'; separate Ervebo + experimental Sudan-ebolavirus observational study starting for frontline workers
source: WHO / Africa CDC / Al Jazeera / STAT News — 12 August–16 September 2026
contestNote: 20 August: WHO and Africa CDC announced the ICG approved immediate release of 70,000 Ervebo (rVSV-ZEBOV) doses to DRC — 20,000 for a Phase 3 clinical trial testing cross-protection against Bundibugyo virus, 50,000 for frontline and health workers. WHO said 16 September that over 3,000 healthcare and frontline workers have now received Ervebo under the compassionate-use campaign DRC launched 27 August, still short of the 50,000-dose target. WHO cautioned it is not known whether Ervebo is protective against Bundibugyo virus in humans, though early lab/animal data suggest possible partial protection. Tedros said 16 September the Phase 3 randomized clinical trial is expected to begin 'within weeks' in Ituri, alongside a separate observational study combining Ervebo with an experimental Sudan-ebolavirus vaccine for frontline workers, due to start later that week or early the following week. Tedros noted two additional candidates (Oxford's ChAdOx1 BDBV in the UK and a Moderna mRNA candidate in Canada) remain in earlier-stage safety trials.
delta: 3,000+ doses administered under compassionate use as of 16 September, up from ~2,000 reported 10 September
deltaNote: The 28 May WHO expert panel ruling barred Ervebo use outside research settings; the 7 August TAG-CVP recommendation, 12 August trial talks, 20 August dose allocation, 27 August compassionate-use campaign launch, and the 16 September 'within weeks' Phase 3 timeline are successive steps toward a structured clinical trial pathway alongside expanding frontline-worker protection. Since the ICG mechanism's 2021 establishment, over 56,000 Ervebo doses have been allocated for DRC outbreaks combined, plus 167,000 doses in preventive campaigns across five countries.

label: DRC Provinces + Countries Affected
value: 62 of 167 health zones across 7 DRC provinces + Uganda (outbreak closed) + France (recovered) + Germany (treated)
source: ECDC Ebola Outbreak Tracker (data as of 16 September) — published 18 September 2026
delta: Health-zone count held at 62 of 167 across all seven provinces (Ituri 28/36, North Kivu 16/34, Tshopo 7/23, Haut-Uélé 6/13, Bas-Uélé 3/11, South Kivu 1/34, Sud-Ubangi 1/16); Africa CDC's Emergency Consultative Group said 17 September the data 'do not yet confirm that the outbreak has reached its peak,' disputing DRC Health Minister Roger Samuel Kamba's claim that growth had already peaked in mid-August
deltaNote: Ituri Province remains the epicenter with the large majority of cases and deaths across 28 of 36 health zones. North Kivu (16 of 34 zones, including Katwa, Biena and Manguredjipa) has the highest fatality rate of any affected province and continues to see rising transmission; officials link the acceleration to M23/government force fighting around Goma. Haut-Uélé, Tshopo, South Kivu and Bas-Uélé round out the six eastern provinces; Sud-Ubangi (first case 9 September, first in western DRC, bordering the Central African Republic and Republic of Congo) is now folded into the 167-zone denominator. Sud-Ubangi's acting governor Jean-René Galekwa Vundawe said 38 contacts of the index patient have been quarantined. Ebola cases were also detected among schoolchildren in Bunia, Ituri, as the 2026-27 school year opened in early September. Uganda's outbreak (Kampala + Wakiso) was declared over by its own Ministry of Health on 28 July and confirmed over by WHO on 25 August after the 42-day monitoring period. Mambasa Territory (IS-controlled) remains largely inaccessible to response teams. WHO's second IHR Emergency Committee meeting (24 August) maintained PHEIC status and expanded 'high risk' guidance to nine bordering states including Burundi and the Central African Republic.

label: Contact Tracing Coverage (DRC)
source: ECDC Ebola outbreak tracker — data as of 16 September 2026 (published 18 September)
delta: National coverage rebounded to 87.6% (16 September) from 78.6% (13 September)
deltaNote: The 16 September update put active follow-up at 87.6% of identified contacts nationally, reversing the nine-point drop recorded 13 September. WHO's 100-day assessment noted tracing coverage had climbed dramatically from just 9% in the outbreak's first week, but the metric has fluctuated week to week (85.7% on 5 Sept → 88.3% on 7 Sept → 84.4% on 9 Sept → 88% on 12 Sept → 78.6% on 13 Sept → 87.6% on 16 Sept). Africa CDC's Emergency Consultative Group cautioned 17 September that high reported contact-tracing percentages may mask gaps in initial contact identification. A recalibrated Lancet Infectious Diseases modelling study put the probability of Ebola spillover into South Sudan at roughly 69.3%, prompting a WHO/UNMISS preparedness mission to the border town of Ezo (27-28 August); no confirmed South Sudan case has been reported as of 16 September. Uganda's contact-tracing program is closed following its outbreak-end declaration, confirmed by WHO on 25 August. Mambasa Territory (IS-controlled) remains a contact-tracing dead zone, and community resistance (isolation refusals, a patient escape in Katwa, blocked ring-closure in Tshopo) is separately undermining follow-up in several provinces.
